transcript.text: Hi there! Let's figure out how your mind works through a quick chat. To start off, when your mind wanders and nothing demands your attention, what do you find yourself thinking about?

Usually, I'm mentally checking off the grocery list for my Tuesday meal prep or tweaking the itinerary for our upcoming family reunion. Honestly, I don't leave much room for empty daydreams because I like keeping my projects moving forward.
It sounds like you really value keeping things organized and moving forward. Tell me about the last time you were around a lot of people for a long time—how did you feel afterwards?

Oh, I loved it—we hosted our annual neighborhood block party this past Saturday, and I was in my element managing the grill schedule and chatting with everyone. Afterwards, I just felt energized and immediately started drafting the thank-you notes and planning next year's layout.

You really thrive on the energy of an event and love taking charge of the details! Tell me about a time you had to give someone feedback or news they wouldn't like. What went through your mind and what did you do?

One of our team leads was consistently missing project deadlines, so I pulled her aside on Monday morning and laid out the exact timeline she needed to meet. There's no point sugarcoating it; I just gave her the hard facts and the new schedule so we could fix the problem and get back on track immediately.
Thanks for sharing how you handled that direct conversation. When you plan a major family trip or move, walk me through how you actually make it happen from start to finish.

I start by creating a color-coded spreadsheet with strict deadlines for every single task, from booking flights to packing boxes. Once the schedule is set, I delegate specific jobs to everyone involved and check in daily to make sure we're all staying ahead of the timeline.
When you try to understand how something complex works for the first time, like a new piece of technology or a complicated recipe, how do you usually go about figuring it out?

I skip right past the fluff and go straight to the instruction manual to read the step-by-step rules. Then I test it out practically, following the established sequence until I've got the process down cold.
